question: Does the already-preregistered top-FFN arm preserve the bounded language screens better than the paid-for Q2.6 full-scope control while retaining quantity and direct replay performance?

matched: quantity corpus, replay slices, source order, and evaluation splits
optimizer schedule, batch size, attempt budgets, and stop conditions
tangent projection, direct per-slice functional replay authority, quantity gates, and selection rule
frozen BLiMP and TinyStories case sets, aggregate thresholds, and evaluator
comparability.only_prospective_training_difference: Q2.7 uses --trainable-scope top-ffn while Q2.6 trained the full model.
invalidators: any drift in a bound artifact hash
any training or selection difference beyond trainable scope
any reuse of BLiMP or TinyStories observations for checkpoint selection
any post-result change to thresholds or outcome rules

prospective_arm.mechanics: unchanged from the bound Q2.7 contract

decision.go: The prospectively selected top-FFN seed-2 candidate passes every quantity, replay, promotion, BLiMP, and TinyStories gate. Conclude only that this scope improved the declared language-preservation trade-off versus the full-scope historical control; consider separately budgeted seeds 1 and 3.
decision.no_go_before_language_gate: No quantity/replay-feasible promoted candidate exists. Retire this top-FFN scope and do not spend the conditional language-gate budget.
decision.no_go_at_language_gate: The promoted candidate fails BLiMP or TinyStories. Retire this top-FFN scope without tuning or repetition.
decision.inconclusive: Infrastructure or integrity failure yields no scientific inference and cannot change the intervention.
claims_forbidden: that top-FFN localization is established by literature
causal attribution to parameter count rather than the tested scope bundle

roi.targeted_review_trigger: Only before introducing a new intervention family such as adapters, masks/pruning, or a different layer boundary, or if this comparability audit is invalidated.
